- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from + to - within 3 days, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid lag.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% to align with historical volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period reversals; if sentiment turns negative after 20–25 days, adjust forecast downward by 2–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
